name: Nature vs Urban Photos: Affect Misattribution Procedure
description:
Faithful replication of the Affect Misattribution Procedure (AMP) of Koivisto & Grassini (2022), "Affective responses to urban but not to natural scenes depend on inter-individual differences in childhood nature exposure", Journal of Environmental Psychology 82, 101840. The photos, Chinese characters, photo–character pairings, noise mask, SAM manikin scales and nature-in-self pictures are the authors' own PsyToolkit materials from OSF autmz (posted without a licence); they are used with credit to the authors and this template will be taken down if the authors object.

What participants do: screening (people who understand Chinese language or characters are excluded, as in the original), age, gender and country. Then two blocks in counterbalanced order, each with 4 practice trials and 40 trials (each of 40 photos once, random order: 20 nature photos of rocks/desert, forest, snow and water, 20 urban photos). Every trial: cue word 1500 ms, blank 500 ms, photo 100 ms, blank 100 ms, Chinese character 100 ms, noise mask 500 ms, blank 500 ms, then SAM valence (1 very unpleasant – 9 very pleasant) and SAM arousal (1 unaroused/calm – 9 aroused/excited), answered by clicking the yellow balls under the manikins. In the indirect block participants rate their reaction to the Chinese character and try to ignore the photo (the AMP); in the direct block they rate their reaction to the photo. Afterwards: Inclusion of Nature in Self (4 picture items, 1–7) and the Nature Exposure Scale now and in childhood (ages 5–10), 6 items each, 1–5.

What the original found (abstract, N = 316): individual factors (childhood and current nature exposure, nature connectedness, gender, age) did not predict immediate affective responses to nature, but childhood nature exposure moderated the reported affect following urban images; the authors suggest an inherited tendency to respond positively to nature, whereas responses to urban scenes depend more on individual experience. In the open data, mean valence was 5.68 after nature vs 5.41 after urban primes in the indirect block, and 7.05 vs 4.22 for the photos themselves in the direct block.

Data: indirect and direct = { valence, arousal } keyed by photo id (dr/fo/sn/wa = nature, ur = urban; shown = photo + character); trial_timing keyed '<block>:<photo id>' = { character, environment, subcategory, prime_ms, soa_ms } measured in the browser; design = { block_order }; ins = { ins1–ins4 }; nes_current = { nesa1–nesa6 }, nes_childhood = { nesc1–nesc6 } (sums = eins, nes_a, nes_b in the original data). Analysis as in the paper: linear mixed models of valence with environment × task and environment × childhood nature exposure, participant and item as random effects.

Differences from the original study: (1) runs in the browser (frame-timed, ~100 ms at 60 Hz, actual durations recorded) instead of PsyToolkit in full-screen mode; (2) no 10-second time limit on the ratings (the original saved 0 for time-outs and dropped them); (3) instruction screens are given as text with the authors' wording instead of the original instruction images, and practice trials are not saved; (4) a typo in one NES label ('Weakly') is shown as 'Weekly'; (5) the 4 INS items are answered by clicking 1–7 under each picture strip instead of typing the number; (6) excluded participants (who understand Chinese) end with the original message and their response is not completed.
author: Koivisto & Grassini

elements.description: Indirect (AMP) block: 40 trials, each photo once in random order, 100 ms photo prime, 100 ms blank, 100 ms Chinese character, 500 ms noise mask; then SAM valence (1 very unpleasant … 9 very pleasant) and arousal (1 unaroused/calm … 9 aroused/excited). key = photo id (dr/fo/sn/wa = nature, ur = urban); shown = [photo, character]. config.description: Affect Misattribution Procedure (AMP) with nature and urban photos, rebuilt from Koivisto & Grassini (2022), Journal of Environmental Psychology 82:101840, with the authors' PsyToolkit materials from OSF autmz. In each trial a photo flashes for 100 ms, then a Chinese character for 100 ms and a noise mask. In the indirect block participants rate their reaction to the Chinese character; in the direct block their reaction to the photo (SAM valence and arousal, 9 points). 40 photos (20 nature, 20 urban), both blocks in counterbalanced order with 4 practice trials each. Then Inclusion of Nature in Self (4 pictures) and the Nature Exposure Scale for now and for childhood.

paper.title: Affective responses to urban but not to natural scenes depend on inter-individual differences in childhood nature exposure
